newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares mixed amidst political worry.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares mixed amidst political worry.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed on Wednesday recovering early losses in what traders said was a technical rebound amidst worries over tensions between Israel and the Palestinians.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.28 percent, or 0.69 points, to 243.20 on an all-share turnover of 110 million shekels against 77 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.26 percent higher at 251.11.

"During the last two weeks the market rose for only two days and now it's time for a technical rebound. It's still too early to talk about a real improvement and investors are worried because of the political uncertainty," said Idan Azoulay at Impact Union.
Israel broke ground on Tuesday for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, raising Israeli-Palestinian tensions.
"It's difficult to say what happened today. The explanation might be that investors simply decided that prices are attractive again," said Dannialla Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities.

"Because of the political situation foreign investors are sitting on the fence waiting...It's interesting to note that foreigners lowered their activity in emerging markets all over the world not only in Israel," Finn added.

Elron Electronic Industries rose 2.25 percent to 4,400 agorot. Lehman Brothers estimated on Wednesday that Elron would earn $0.86 a share in 1998. Lehman maintained its 2-Outperform rating for the company.

The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which plunged 4.25 percent to 18,443 agorot on volume of 17.5 million shekels. Teva said on Wednesday reports the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) ordered changes in the labelling of the company's Copaxone drug were unfounded.
Teva's Nasdaq share price fell 6.2 percent on Tuesday to 53 15/16. Dillon, Read & Co in a report on Wednesday attributed the fall to the rumours.
Other active shares included Bank Leumi, which rose 2.25 percent to 537 agorot on turnover of 5 million shekels and Supersol which surged 4.75 percent to 965 agorot on volume of 4 million shekels.
Traders said Supersol's rise was only a technical correction. The share lost more than 10 percent since the beginning of the month.
